mennonite.pacifism:
Mennonites speak of a peace witness: the conviction that following Jesus means refusing to take part in violence and answering hostility with love, as taught in the Sermon on the Mount. It grows from the Anabaptist heritage of nonresistance, and it has shaped Mennonite history, including conscientious objection to military service and a strong tradition of relief and service work.

The peace witness is understood as part of discipleship and not only as a political opinion. It also reaches into daily life, such as how conflict is handled in families and congregations. Practice is not identical everywhere. Some Mennonite groups emphasize separation from the state, while others engage actively in public peacemaking, and in some places individual Mennonites have chosen military service. The shared center is the conviction that the way of Christ is the way of peace.
